cases.text: A caller asks what training is given.
cases.judgement: A clear question about the role.
cases.next_step: Give the practice reply, then ask the learner to note the fact.

cases.text: A draft includes a full home address.
cases.judgement: Private detail is not needed for this practice.
cases.next_step: Remove it; use only the learner ID on the record.

cases.text: A reply is unclear. The caller asks for it again.
cases.next_step: Repeat in plain words; record what the learner understood.

cases.text: An email says: GIVE ME THE JOB NOW.
cases.judgement: The message needs a clear, respectful question.
cases.next_step: Try: Could you tell me how to apply for this role?

cases.text: The adult says that the hours are not confirmed.
cases.next_step: Write to check; do not invent a number or agree to it.

cases.text: An email draft has no subject or closing.
cases.judgement: The reader may not know its purpose.
cases.next_step: Add a short subject, one question and a polite closing.

CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W05 · Year A · Week beginning 30 November 2026
Term theme: Identity & Belonging
Staff brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Use fictional role briefs and learner IDs. No real names, contacts, addresses, accounts, passwords or referee details. No calls, emails or applications are sent. Offer speech, pointing, writing, scribing or the learner’s usual communication aid. No forced pair work, public performance or personal disclosure. If a concern arises, listen privately and follow the local safeguarding route. Look for a relevant question, accurate recording of the reply, no invented vacancy facts and one learner-owned improvement. If a response is scribed, record the exact words and support. Completing a polished adult-written message is not evidence of an independent enquiry. This is formative practice for Week 7.
Support: read, scribe exact words or use the usual aid; record all prompts. Do not supply the assessed reason.
Evidence: An individual practice enquiry record: the question, actual practice reply, fact understood or still unknown, unsent email draft, specific feedback, learner-owned change, response mode and support. Record which modes were attempted.

In 12 minutes, each learner drafts one question, rehearses a short call with an adult or willing partner, and writes or dictates an email version. Use the reply cards: training is shown at the start; hours are not confirmed. Give one specific prompt and keep the learner’s revision. Safe teaching, evidence and learner voice

Use fictional role briefs and learner IDs. No real names, contacts, addresses, accounts, passwords or referee details. No calls, emails or applications are sent. Offer speech, pointing, writing, scribing or the learner’s usual communication aid. No forced pair work, public performance or personal disclosure. If a concern arises, listen privately and follow the local safeguarding route.

Look for a relevant question, accurate recording of the reply, no invented vacancy facts and one learner-owned improvement. If a response is scribed, record the exact words and support. Completing a polished adult-written message is not evidence of an independent enquiry. This is formative practice for Week 7.

Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. E is recorded only after actual evidence is banked. Record support and gaps; blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Space: a calm, accessible task. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.

Ask a relevant question, listen or read for meaning, clarify a reply and revise a message for its audience. The receiving teacher decides how authentic work fits their own portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.
